mcat_description.short: Eco Portable Cabins are prefabricated, relocatable structures built with eco-friendly or sustainable materials such as FRP (Fibre Reinforced Plastic), PUF/EPS sandwich panels, or recyclable steel frames, sold as complete ready-to-install units for site offices, security posts, accommodation, and commercial use.
mcat_description.long: Eco Portable Cabins are factory-manufactured, modular prefabricated structures distinguished from standard portable cabins by their use of sustainable or low-impact construction materials — primarily FRP panels, PUF/EPS insulated sandwich panels, GI/PPGL colour-coated sheets, and recyclable mild steel frames. They are designed for rapid on-site deployment, relocation, and reuse, making them a preferred choice for construction site offices, labour accommodation, security guard posts, eco-tourism resorts, and temporary commercial setups such as cafes and kiosks. Structural configurations range from compact single-room security cabins to multi-room double-storey portable houses, with dimensions typically spanning 4×4 ft to 40×10 ft and wall panel thicknesses of 50–75 mm. In the Indian B2B market, buyers specify material type (FRP vs PUF vs sandwich panel), cabin dimensions, insulation grade, and end-use application as primary purchase criteria.

market_context: In the Indian B2B market, 'Eco Portable Cabins' is a commercially recognised sub-category of portable/prefabricated cabins distinguished by the use of sustainable or low-environmental-impact materials — primarily FRP (Fibre Reinforced Plastic), PUF (Polyurethane Foam) sandwich panels, EPS panels, and recyclable GI/MS steel frames. FRP is the dominant eco-material in this segment, valued for its light weight, corrosion resistance, and low maintenance; PUF sandwich panels are preferred for thermally demanding applications such as site offices in extreme climates. Multiple Indian manufacturers (EPACK Prefab, Spangle Steel, Fibrecrafts India, Needhi FRP, Zinto Cabins, Orchid Cabins) actively market products under the 'eco portable cabin' or 'FRP eco cabin' label. The category spans a wide application range — from compact 4×4 ft security guard cabins to 40×10 ft double-storey portable houses — with customisation of dimensions, insulation grade, flooring, and electrical fittings being standard practice. Buyers in this segment are primarily construction contractors, industrial facility managers, eco-tourism operators, and government/PSU procurement teams. The 'eco' designation in Indian trade vocabulary signals material sustainability and energy efficiency (insulation reducing HVAC load), not a formal green certification standard. Unit quoting is per piece for standard sizes and per sq ft for custom builds — both conventions are active in the market.
